definition_zh: 古董；古物；古老的；古董的
definition_en: an object from an earlier period valued for its age, or an adjective describing such objects
core_image: 旧货店里落着薄尘的黄铜座钟
scene: 街角的小店摆满旧家具，铜器泛着暗光。She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
sceneCN: 这里 antique 是「古董的」（第 2 个义项：形容年代久远且有价值的物品）；句意是她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。

derivatives.zh: 名词：古代；古物，同源于拉丁语 antiquus
形容词：过时的；陈旧的
形容词：研究古物（收藏）的

senses.title: An object from the past
senses.definition: a piece of furniture, jewellery, or other object that is old and valued for its age
senses.definitionCN: 年代久远、因年代而受珍视的家具、首饰或其他物件
senses.example: She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。
senses.why: Latin antiquus meant 'former, ancient', and the noun use in English picked out objects that survive from that former time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antiquus 意为「从前的、古老的」，英语里的名词用法挑出的就是从那个从前留存下来的物件。

senses.title: Belonging to an earlier period
senses.definition: used of furniture, objects, or styles that come from an earlier age
senses.definitionCN: 用于来自较早时代的家具、物件或样式
senses.example: The room was full of antique furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里摆满了古董家具。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain temporal meaning of antiquus, so anything surviving from an earlier age can be called antique.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了 antiquus 单纯的时间含义，因此任何从较早年代留存下来的东西都能叫 antique。

senses.title: Old-fashioned, out of date
senses.definition: used in a slightly mocking way for ideas or methods that belong to the past
senses.definitionCN: 略带嘲意地指属于过去的思想或方法
senses.example: His antique views on marriage surprised the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他对婚姻的陈旧看法让全班很吃惊。
senses.why: Once a thing is old enough to be quaint, the same word can belittle an idea as a museum piece.
senses.whyCN: 当一样东西旧到显得古怪时，同一个词也能把某种观念贬为博物馆里的陈列品。

intro.en: Antique descends from a Latin word for 'former' built on ante, 'before'.
intro.cn: antique 来自拉丁语中表示「从前的」的词，词根是 ante「在前」。

items.en: ante meant 'before' and remains in words such as anterior.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前」，仍见于 anterior 等词。

items.en: antiquus meant 'old, former, of long ago'.
items.cn: antiquus 意为「旧的、从前的、很久以前的」。

items.en: Old French antique passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语 antique 把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: English first used antique of ancient times and old remains.
items.cn: 英语 antique 最初用于古代与古代遗存。

items.en: By the nineteenth century antique had narrowed to valued old objects and their style.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，antique 已收窄为指受珍视的旧物及其风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for old; the near-meaning group is other words for things from the past.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「旧」的拉丁词根；近义组是其他指旧物的词。

entries.definition: the ancient past, or an object from it
old and no longer useful
being the only one of its kind
entries.definitionCN: 独特的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: old but of good quality, especially clothing or wine
an object surviving from the past
an object valued by collectors

normalIntro.en: Antique means old enough to be kept and valued.
normalIntro.cn: antique 就是旧到值得被收藏珍视。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable: an-TIQUE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：an-TIQUE。

normal.en: An antique is a thing; antique as an adjective describes it.
normal.cn: antique 作名词指物件，作形容词则表示「古董的」。

normal.en: Antique shop and antique furniture are the two most common pairs.
normal.cn: antique shop 与 antique furniture 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Antiquity is the abstract noun; antique is the object.
normal.cn: antiquity 是抽象名词，antique 指具体物件。

normal.en: Do not spell it antic; the que comes from French.
normal.cn: 不要写成 antic，词尾 que 来自法语。

abstract.cn: 想象黄铜钟面上的一层薄尘。

abstract.en: See a price tag tied with old string.
abstract.cn: 想象用旧绳系着的价签。

abstract.en: See a modern chair beside a carved wooden one.
abstract.cn: 想象现代椅子旁边那把雕花木椅。

examples.cn: 她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。

examples.cn: 房间里摆满了古董家具。

examples.en: His antique views on marriage surprised the class.
examples.cn: 他对婚姻的陈旧看法让全班很吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: anti（前）加 -que：从前留下来的东西，就是古董。

root: 来自拉丁语 antiquus「古代的、从前的」，由 ante「在前」加词尾构成，经古法语 antique 进入英语；同根词有 antiquity、antiquated、antiquarian。

sensesIntro.en: The same age-word names an old object, describes an old style, and mocks an outdated idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「旧」词既能指旧物，也能形容旧样式，还能嘲讽过时的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass clock that has outlived its first owners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只比最初主人活得更久的黄铜钟。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of age that English uses as both noun and adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示年代的拉丁语形容词，英语中兼作名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root antiquus also gives antiquity and antiquated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 antiquus 也派生出 antiquity 与 antiquated。

items.meaning: old but fine, as of wine

definition_zh: 焦虑的；担忧的；渴望的；急切的
definition_en: worried about something uncertain, or very eager to do or get something
core_image: 候诊室里捏皱的挂号单
scene: 手术室外的走廊上，家属一遍遍看墙上的钟。The family grew anxious as the hours passed.
sceneCN: 这里 anxious 是「焦虑的」（第 1 个义项：对不确定之事感到担忧）；句意是随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。

pos.zh: 形容词：焦虑的；担忧的；渴望的

derivatives.zh: 名词：焦虑；忧虑
副词：焦虑地；急切地
名词：焦虑的状态

senses.title: Worried about something
senses.definition: feeling uneasy because you do not know how something will turn out
senses.definitionCN: 因为不知道事情会怎样发展而感到不安
senses.example: The family grew anxious as the hours passed.
senses.exampleCN: 随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。
senses.why: The Latin ancestor angere meant 'to squeeze', and anxius described a person whose chest feels constricted; anxious keeps that bodily tightness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 angere 意为「挤压」，anxius 形容胸口发紧的人；anxious 保留了这种身体上的紧绷感。

senses.title: Very eager to do something
senses.definition: wanting very much to do something or for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 非常想做某事，或非常希望某事发生
senses.example: She was anxious to finish the report before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她急于在中午前完成报告。
senses.why: Strong desire tightens the mind in much the same way as fear, so anxious for and anxious to express eagerness rather than dread.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的愿望让心里绷紧的方式与恐惧相似，所以 anxious for 与 anxious to 表达的是急切而不是害怕。

intro.en: Anxious is the adjective built on the Latin root for a tightened chest.
intro.cn: anxious 是建立在拉丁语「胸口收紧」词根上的形容词。

items.en: angere meant 'to squeeze or choke'.
items.cn: angere 意为「挤压、使窒息」。

items.en: anxius meant 'uneasy, distressed'.
items.cn: anxius 意为「不安的、苦恼的」。

items.en: The noun anxietas named the state of worry.
items.cn: 名词 anxietas 指忧虑的状态。

items.en: English anxious first meant 'greatly troubled'.
items.cn: 英语 anxious 最初意为「极为烦恼的」。

items.en: The sense of eager desire became common in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「急切渴望」的义项在十九世纪变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Latin anxiety family; the near-meaning group gives other worried words.
note.cn: 形近组同属拉丁语焦虑词族；近义组是其他表示担忧的词。

in a worried way
severe mental pain

jumpy and uneasy

normalIntro.en: Anxious is a squeezed chest, whether from fear or from wanting.
normalIntro.cn: anxious 是收紧的胸口，可能因为害怕，也可能因为渴望。

normal.en: Anxious about a problem, anxious to do something.
normal.cn: 对问题用 anxious about，急于做事用 anxious to。

normal.en: The noun is anxiety, not anxiousness in most writing.
normal.cn: 多数书面语中名词用 anxiety，而不用 anxiousness。

normal.en: Anxious for news means waiting eagerly for it.
normal.cn: anxious for news 意为急切等待消息。

normal.en: The x sounds like ks: ANK-shus.
normal.cn: x 读作 ks 的音：ANK-shus。

normal.en: Do not confuse anxious with anger; the root is shared but the meaning is not.
normal.cn: 不要把它与 anger 混为一谈，词根相关但含义不同。

abstract.cn: 想象候诊室里被捏皱的单据。

abstract.en: See eyes fixed on a corridor clock.
abstract.cn: 想象盯着走廊时钟的眼睛。

abstract.en: See a hand raised long before the question ends.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没说完就举起的手。

examples.cn: 随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。

examples.en: He felt anxious about the interview all week.
examples.cn: 整整一周他都在为面试担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: anx（紧）加 -ious（……的）：心里发紧的，就是焦虑的。

root: 来自拉丁语 anxius「不安的」，源于 angere「挤压、扼住」，与 anxiety、anguish 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The same tightness serves fear about the future and eagerness for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种紧绷既用于对未来的恐惧，也用于对未来的渴望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand crushing a waiting-room ticket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把候诊单攥皱。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of tension that still carries a physical feel.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示紧绷的拉丁形容词，至今仍带着身体感。

latinIntro.en: The squeeze root angere underlies anxious, anxiety, and anguish.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「挤压」的词根 angere 贯穿 anxious、anxiety 与 anguish。

definition_zh: 道歉；歉意；辩解；（贫乏的）勉强替代
definition_en: a statement saying you are sorry, a defence of something, or a very poor example of something
core_image: 一封写满「对不起」的短信
scene: 桌上放着一张手写的纸条，第一行就是抱歉的话。He sent a short apology the next day.
sceneCN: 这里 apology 是「道歉」（第 1 个义项：为过错表达歉意的话）；句意是他第二天发来一封简短的道歉信。

derivatives.zh: 动词：道歉
形容词：歉意的
名词：辩护者

senses.title: A statement of regret
senses.definition: words saying that you are sorry for something you did
senses.definitionCN: 为做过的事表示抱歉的话
senses.example: He sent a short apology the next day.
senses.exampleCN: 他第二天发来一封简短的道歉信。
senses.why: Greek apologia was a speech in defence; English apology kept the 'speech' part and moved from defending oneself to admitting fault.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 apologia 是辩护的言辞；英语 apology 保留了「言辞」这一部分，并从为自己辩护转为承认过失。

senses.title: A defence of a position
senses.definition: a formal argument in support of a belief, person, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 为某种信念、人物或制度所作的正式论证
senses.example: The book is an apology for classical education.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是为古典教育辩护之作。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense, kept alive in learned writing and in the word apologetics.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语本义，在学术写作与 apologetics 一词中仍然存活。

senses.title: A very poor example
senses.definition: used in the phrase a poor apology for to mock something that barely deserves the name
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a poor apology for 短语，嘲讽某物几乎配不上这个名称
senses.example: The hut was a poor apology for a hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 那间小屋勉强算个旅馆。
senses.why: If an apology is words offered in place of a fault, then a poor apology for a thing is a weak substitute standing in for the real one.
senses.whyCN: 如果 apology 是拿来顶替过失的话，那么对某物而言 a poor apology for 就是顶替真货的蹩脚替代品。

intro.en: Apology is a Greek defence speech that turned into an admission of fault.
intro.cn: apology 原是一篇希腊语的辩护辞，后来变成承认过失。

items.en: apo meant 'away from'.
items.cn: apo 意为「离开」。

items.en: logos meant 'speech, account'.
items.cn: logos 意为「言辞、论述」。

items.en: apologia was a speech made in defence.
items.cn: apologia 是一篇辩护之辞。

items.en: English apology first meant a formal defence.
items.cn: 英语 apology 最初意为正式辩护。

items.en: The everyday sense of saying sorry became dominant in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 「道歉」这一日常义在十八世纪占了主导。

note.en: The look-alike group is the apology family; the near-meaning group gives other responses to a fault.
note.cn: 形近组是 apology 词族；近义组是其他面对过失的回应。

showing regret
the defence of a faith
a reason offered to lessen blame

normalIntro.en: An apology is a speech that answers a fault.
normalIntro.cn: apology 就是回应过失的一番话。

normal.en: Make an apology is more formal than say sorry.
normal.cn: make an apology 比 say sorry 更正式。

normal.en: Apologies for the delay is a common written opener.
normal.cn: apologies for the delay 是常见的书面开头。

normal.en: An apology for a hotel means a very bad hotel.
normal.cn: an apology for a hotel 意为极差的旅馆。

normal.en: The plural apologies is used in formal notices.
normal.cn: 复数 apologies 常用于正式告示。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-POL-o-gy.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-POL-o-gy。

abstract.cn: 想象桌上折好的纸条。

abstract.en: See a lawyer's long speech in an old court.
abstract.cn: 想象旧法庭上律师的长篇陈词。

abstract.en: See a cardboard box called a house.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被当作房子的纸箱。

examples.en: He sent a short apology the next day.
examples.cn: 他第二天发来一封简短的道歉信。

examples.en: The book is an apology for classical education.
examples.cn: 这本书是为古典教育辩护之作。

examples.en: The hut was a poor apology for a hotel.
examples.cn: 那间小屋勉强算个旅馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: apo（离开）加 log（说）加 -y：把过错说开的话，道歉。

root: 来自希腊语 apologia「辩护之辞」，由 apo「离开」与 logos「言辞」构成，经拉丁语 apologia 进入英语；由辩护义转为道歉义。

sensesIntro.en: A defence speech becomes an admission of fault, and then a mocking label for a poor substitute.
sensesIntro.cn: 辩护之辞先变成认错的话，再变成对蹩脚替代品的嘲讽说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words offered to answer for a fault.
core.cn: 核心意象：为过失作出交代的一番话。

intro.en: A Greek compound noun whose two parts remain productive in English.
intro.cn: 这是一个希腊语复合名词，两个成分在英语里仍有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun unchanged as apologia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样借入希腊名词作 apologia。

items.meaning: a defence, later an expression of regret

definition_zh: 为特定用途配置的一整套器械或装置；也可指机构、组织等抽象体系
definition_en: a set of equipment assembled for a particular purpose, or an organized system such as a state or party structure
core_image: 实验台上，玻璃管、支架、气瓶与阀门连成一套，每一段都扣在指定的位置，只为完成一次反应
scene: 潜水前，队员检查背上的气瓶、减压阀与面罩，确认每一处接头都不漏气。The diver checked the breathing apparatus before the descent.
sceneCN: 这里指成套的呼吸装置（第 2 个义项：为潜水或消防配置的呼吸器）；句意：潜水员在下潜前检查了呼吸装置。

derivatives.zh: 由「装置」加英语复数词尾构成，义为「多套装置」
由拉丁语「预先准备」经法语进入英语，义为「准备」
由「准备」加名词词尾构成，义为「准备、制备」
由「准备」加形容词词尾构成，义为「预备的」
由拉丁语「重新准备」经法语进入英语，义为「修理」

senses.title: A set assembled for an experiment
senses.titleCN: 为实验组装的一套器械
senses.definition: the connected pieces of equipment set up to carry out a particular experiment or operation
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项实验或操作而连接起来的一套器材
senses.example: The whole apparatus was rebuilt after the glass tube broke.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃管破裂后，整套装置被重新组装。
senses.why: Apparatus names a prepared set, not a single tool, because its root verb means to make ready.
senses.whyCN: 「装置」指准备好的一套，而不是单件工具，因为其词根动词意为「准备」。

senses.title: Breathing gear
senses.definition: the cylinder, regulator and mask that let a person breathe under water, in smoke or at altitude
senses.definitionCN: 让人在水下、烟雾中或高空呼吸的气瓶、调节器与面罩组合
senses.example: Firefighters carry breathing apparatus into every smoke-filled room.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员进入每个烟雾弥漫的房间都携带呼吸器。
senses.why: A life-support set is prepared before entry, so the general word attaches to this specialised kit.
senses.whyCN: 生命维持装备要在进入前准备好，因此这个泛称也附着于这套专用器材。

senses.title: The machinery of an organization
senses.definition: the offices, departments and procedures through which a state, party or large body acts
senses.definitionCN: 国家、政党或大型团体赖以行动的机关、部门与程序
senses.example: The reform aimed at the party apparatus rather than at voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革针对的是政党机构，而不是选民。
senses.why: An organisation acts through prepared parts, so the tool word becomes a metaphor for institutional machinery.
senses.whyCN: 组织通过准备好的各个部件行动，于是工具词变成了机构机械的比喻。

senses.title: Gymnastic equipment
senses.definition: the fixed or portable frames and bars used in gymnastics, such as the rings or parallel bars
senses.definitionCN: 体操中使用的固定或可移动框架与横杆，如吊环或双杠
senses.example: The hall's apparatus was inspected before the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前，馆内的体操器械接受了检查。
senses.why: Sporting equipment is also a prepared set, so the word serves for bars, rings and beams.
senses.whyCN: 运动器材同样是准备好的一套，因此这个词也用于横杆、吊环与平衡木。

senses.title: Optical or measuring setup
senses.definition: a bench of lenses, mirrors, lasers and detectors aligned for one measurement
senses.definitionCN: 为一次测量而对准的透镜、反射镜、激光器与探测器组合
senses.example: The optical apparatus had to stay aligned within a micron.
senses.exampleCN: 这套光学装置必须在微米范围内保持对准。
senses.why: Precision work needs many parts fixed in relation to one another, which is exactly what apparatus means.
senses.whyCN: 精密工作需要许多部件按相对位置固定，这正是「装置」所指。

senses.title: Textual collation notes
senses.definition: the recorded variants and editorial notes that accompany a scholarly edition of a text
senses.definitionCN: 学术版本正文旁记录的异文与编者说明
senses.example: The critical apparatus lists every manuscript reading.
senses.exampleCN: 校勘资料列出了每种抄本的读法。
senses.why: Scholars prepare a text with supporting parts, and the old word for equipment names those supporting notes.
senses.whyCN: 学者为正文准备支撑材料，古老的「装备」一词便用来指这些辅助记录。

senses.title: The assembly of a machine
senses.definition: the connected parts of a machine considered as one working whole
senses.definitionCN: 把一台机器的各连接部件视为一个运作整体
senses.example: The valve is only one part of the pumping apparatus.
senses.exampleCN: 阀门只是泵送装置的一部分。

intro.en: Apparatus is a Latin noun for equipment, built on a verb meaning to prepare; English borrowed it whole, including its Latin plural.
intro.cn: 「装置」是拉丁语中表示装备的名词，建立在表示「准备」的动词上；英语整体借入，连拉丁语复数形式也一并保留。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare, make ready or furnish; it is the direct Latin source, while its deeper origin is uncertain and the link to a producing root is only a suggestion.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语动词指准备、备好或供给；它是本词的直接拉丁语来源，其更早来源存疑，与表示「产出」之古词根的关联仅为推测。

items.en: The prefix ad-, meaning toward, combined with parare to give apparare, to get ready for a purpose.
items.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀与「准备」结合，构成「为某目的做好准备」的动词。

items.en: Apparatus was the result noun: the state of being prepared and the set of things prepared, especially for a task.
items.cn: 这个词是结果名词，指准备好的状态以及准备好的一套东西，尤指为某项任务所备。

items.en: The Latin fourth-declension noun kept the same form in the plural, and English still allows apparatus as a plural.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语第四变格名词的复数与原形同形，英语至今仍允许用原形作复数。

items.era: ENGLISH BORROWING · FIRST RECORD DATE UNCERTAIN
items.en: English took the word in the seventeenth century for a prepared set of instruments, especially in science; the exact year of the borrowing is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个词，指准备好的一套器具，尤用于科学；具体借入年代不确定。

items.en: The same picture of prepared parts was later applied to state and party machinery and to the notes that support an edited text.
items.cn: 同一幅「准备好的部件」画面后来被用于国家与政党机构，以及支撑校勘版本的注释。

note.en: The first group shares the prepare root; the second group separates the four kit words.
note.cn: 第一组共享「准备」词根；第二组区分四个器械名词。

entries.definition: The English plural, used when several separate sets are counted.
entries.definitionCN: 英语复数，用于清点几套分开的装置。

entries.definition: To make ready; the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 做好准备；名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: The act of making ready; it stresses the process, not the set.
entries.definitionCN: 准备的动作；强调过程而非成套之物。

entries.definition: To make ready again; it shares the prepare root with a again-prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 重新备好；共享「准备」词根并带「再次」前缀。

entries.definition: A bought or issued set of machines and tools; apparatus is assembled for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 采购或配发的成套机器工具；装置是为任务组装起来的。

entries.definition: One precision measuring tool; apparatus is the whole setup around it.
entries.definitionCN: 单件精密测量器具；装置是围绕它的整套布置。

entries.definition: The installed system of measuring and control devices in a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 工厂中安装的测量与控制仪表系统。

entries.definition: An improvised or temporary setup; apparatus is more deliberate and complete.
entries.definitionCN: 临时拼搭的装置；目标词更像有意搭成的完整一套。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root verb means to prepare, so apparatus is the set made ready.
normal.cn: 词根动词意为准备，因此装置就是准备好的一套。

normal.en: The family runs prepare, preparation, preparatory, repair and apparatus.
normal.cn: 同族词包括准备、制备、预备的、修理与装置。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: laboratory apparatus, breathing apparatus, state apparatus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：实验装置、呼吸器、国家机构。

normal.en: The Latin plural is the same word, though English also allows apparatuses.
normal.cn: 拉丁语复数与原形同形，英语也允许加复数词尾。

normal.en: Its cousins are equipment, instrument, instrumentation and rig.
normal.cn: 它的近亲是设备、仪器、仪表系统与临时装置。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every glass tube knows exactly where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每根玻璃管都清楚自己该在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a mask that turns a hostile environment into breathable air.
abstract.cn: 想象一副面罩，把恶劣环境变成可呼吸的空气。

abstract.en: Picture a building full of offices acting like one prepared machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋装满办公室的建筑，像一台准备好的机器那样运作。

examples.en: The apparatus must be assembled in the order given in the manual.
examples.cn: 这套装置必须按手册给定的顺序组装。

examples.en: The state apparatus moved faster than the ministry itself.
examples.cn: 国家机构比部委本身行动得更快。

examples.en: A broken seal can ruin an entire breathing apparatus.
examples.cn: 一处密封破损就能毁掉整套呼吸装置。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: parts prepared and joined for a purpose. The purpose may be an experiment, breathing, sport, measurement, scholarship or the action of an organization.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念：部件为某目的备好并连接起来。这个目的可以是实验、呼吸、运动、测量、校勘，或一个组织的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench of parts clipped into place, each in its fixed position, ready for one operation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台面部件被扣在各自固定位置，为一套操作准备就绪。

branches.en: THE CORE: an assembled set for an experiment, and the working parts of a machine.
branches.cn: 核心：为实验组装的整套器械，以及机器的工作部件。

branches.en: THE LIFE-SUPPORT VERSION: cylinders, regulators and masks.
branches.cn: 生命维持版本：气瓶、调节器与面罩。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL VERSION: the offices and procedures of a state or party.
branches.cn: 机构版本：国家或政党的机关与程序。

branches.en: THE SPORT AND DARKROOM VERSION: rings, bars, enlargers and trays.
branches.cn: 运动与暗房版本：吊环、横杆、放大机与药盘。

branches.en: THE PRECISION AND SCHOLARLY VERSION: aligned optical benches and collation notes.
branches.cn: 精密与学术版本：对准的光学台与校勘注释。

intro.cn: 这个词完全来自拉丁语：一个「准备」动词、一个表目的前缀与一个结果名词。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；表面上的
definition_en: easy to see or understand, or seeming true without being so
core_image: 水面上露出的冰山一角
scene: 会议室的空气一下子僵住，谁都看得出出了问题。It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 apparent 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易看出来）；句意是显然出了什么问题。

pos.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

derivatives.zh: 副词：显然；据说
名词：外观；出现
名词：幽灵；幻象

senses.title: Clearly visible or understood
senses.definition: easy to notice or understand from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 根据证据很容易被察觉或理解
senses.example: It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 显然出了什么问题。
senses.why: Latin apparere meant 'to come into view', built from ad, 'to', and parere, 'to appear'; what is apparent has come into sight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apparere 意为「进入视野」，由 ad「向」与 parere「出现」构成；apparent 就是已经进入视线的东西。

senses.title: Seeming rather than real
senses.definition: true as far as one can see, but possibly not in fact
senses.definitionCN: 就所见而言成立，但事实上未必如此
senses.example: The apparent calm hid a great deal of anger.
senses.exampleCN: 表面上的平静掩藏着极大的愤怒。
senses.why: Because appearing is not the same as being, apparent can warn that the surface may deceive.
senses.whyCN: 因为「显现」不等于「实有」，所以 apparent 可以提醒表面可能欺人。

intro.en: Apparent comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to come into view'.

definition_zh: 呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力；吸引
definition_en: to make an urgent request, to ask a court to change a decision, or to be attractive to someone
core_image: 人群前举起的一只求助的手
scene: 洪水过后，村长站在废墟前向外界求援。The village appealed for food and clean water.
sceneCN: 这里 appeal 是「呼吁；恳求」（第 1 个义项：紧急请求帮助）；句意是村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。

pos.zh: 动词：呼吁；恳求；上诉；有吸引力

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有吸引力的

senses.title: To ask urgently for help
senses.definition: to ask strongly and publicly for something needed
senses.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地请求所需之物
senses.example: The village appealed for food and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。
senses.why: Latin appellare meant 'to address, call upon', from ad, 'to', and pellere, 'to drive'; an appeal drives words toward someone who can act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appellare 意为「向……讲话、呼唤」，由 ad「向」与 pellere「推动」构成；appeal 就是把话推向能行动的人。

senses.title: To ask a court to reconsider
senses.definition: to take a legal decision to a higher court for review
senses.definitionCN: 把法律裁决提交上级法院复审
senses.example: They appealed against the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对判决提出上诉。
senses.why: The idea of calling upon a higher authority fits the courtroom: the losing side calls on a higher court.
senses.whyCN: 「向更高权威求助」的观念正适用于法庭：败诉一方向更高一级法院发出请求。

senses.title: To be attractive
senses.definition: to please or interest someone, often because it suits their needs
senses.definitionCN: 使人喜欢或感兴趣，常因契合其需要
senses.example: The simple design appeals to young buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 简洁的设计吸引了年轻买家。
senses.why: Something that appeals to you calls out to your taste, so the word moved from a spoken request to a silent attraction.
senses.whyCN: appeal to 你的东西是在向你的品味发出呼唤，所以这个词从口头请求延伸为无声的吸引。

items.en: antiquus meant 'former, ancient', from ante 'before'.
items.cn: antiquus 意为「从前的、古代的」，由 ante「在前」构成。

items.en: Latin antiquarius meant 'pertaining to ancient things', used of those who studied them.
items.cn: 拉丁语 antiquarius 意为「与古代事物有关的」，用于指研究古物的人。

items.en: English took antiquary directly from Latin in the sixteenth century for scholars of the past.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入 antiquary，指研究往昔的学者。

items.en: The longer form antiquarian now carries most everyday use, while antiquary survives in learned circles.

normalIntro.en: Antiquary is the person behind the antique shop counter.
normalIntro.cn: antiquary 就是古董店柜台后面那个人。

normal.en: antiqu- means old; -ary marks a person devoted to it.
normal.cn: antiqu- 表示「古老」，-ary 表示「从事者」。

normal.en: An antiquary studies what an antique shop sells.
normal.cn: antiquary 研究的正是古董店出售的东西。

normal.en: The plural antiquaries ends in -ies, like library to libraries.
normal.cn: 复数 antiquaries 把 y 变 ies，与 library 的变化相同。

normal.en: Antiquarian is the long form; antiquary is the short one.

abstract.en: See a magnifying glass over a worn coin.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜下的一枚磨损旧币。

abstract.en: See shelves of leather books, all older than the house.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排比房子还古老的皮面书。

abstract.en: See a soft brush sweeping dust from a relic.
abstract.cn: 想象软毛刷拂去遗物上的灰尘。

examples.cn: 这位古物研究者花了几十年为中世纪印章编目。

examples.en: She bought the map from an antiquary in the old quarter.
examples.cn: 她从老城区一位古董商那里买下了这张地图。

examples.en: Local antiquaries helped preserve the ruined abbey.

definition_zh: 使过时；使陈旧；废弃
definition_en: to make something old-fashioned or obsolete
core_image: 新机器落成，旧齿轮被推到墙角落灰
scene: 新流水线刚启动，几台老机器被推进库房。Digital printing antiquated the old press within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 antiquate 是「使过时」（第 1 个义项：使某物变得陈旧无用）；句意为数码印刷在十年内让那台旧印刷机过时了。

senses.title: To make old-fashioned
senses.definition: to cause something to become outdated or no longer useful
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得过时或不再有用
senses.example: New safety rules antiquated the factory's old wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 新的安全法规使工厂的旧线路过时了。
senses.why: The stem antiquus means 'old', and the verb ending -ate turns the adjective into an action: to give something the quality of being old.
senses.whyCN: 词干 antiquus 意为「旧的」，动词后缀 -ate 把形容词变成动作：让某物带上「旧」的性质。

senses.title: To abolish or discard as outdated
senses.definition: to put an end to a custom or practice because it belongs to the past
senses.definitionCN: 因属于过去而终止某项习俗或做法
senses.example: The council voted to antiquate the outdated toll.
senses.exampleCN: 议会投票废止了那项过时的通行费。
senses.why: Once something is stamped as old, the next step is to push it out of use entirely.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物被贴上「旧」的标签，下一步就是把它彻底弃置不用。

intro.en: Antiquate is a Latin-style verb built on antiquus 'old', meaning literally 'to make old'.
intro.cn: antiquate 是按拉丁动词模式以 antiquus「旧的」构成的词，字面意为「使变旧」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ant- meant 'front, before'.

items.en: antiquus meant 'former, ancient', from ante 'before'.
items.cn: antiquus 意为「从前的、古代的」，源自 ante「在前」。

items.en: Medieval Latin antiquare meant 'to make old or obsolete'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 antiquare 意为「使变旧、使作废」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth or seventeenth century, mostly in learned prose.
items.cn: 英语在十六至十七世纪借入这个动词，主要用于书面语。

items.en: The plain verb is now rare; its participle antiquated does nearly all the work as an adjective.
items.cn: 动词原形如今已少见；其过去分词 antiquated 作为形容词承担了几乎全部用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the antiqu- stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of making things out of date.
note.cn: 形近组共享 antiqu- 词干；近义组收各种「使过时」的动词。

normalIntro.en: Antiquate literally means to make a thing old.
normalIntro.cn: antiquate 的字面义就是「把东西变旧」。

normal.en: antiqu- means old; -ate makes verbs like activate.
normal.cn: antiqu- 表示「旧」，-ate 构成动词，如同 activate。

normal.en: The participle antiquated is the form you will actually meet.
normal.cn: 你实际遇到的多是分词形式 antiquated。

normal.en: Antiquated equipment and antiquated laws are the classic pairs.
normal.cn: antiquated equipment 与 antiquated laws 是经典搭配。

normal.en: Do not confuse antiquate with antique: one is a verb, one a noun.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 antiquate（动词）与 antique（名词）。

normal.en: Antiquation is the abstract noun for the process.
normal.cn: antiquation 是表示这一过程的抽象名词。

abstract.en: See a new machine pushing an old gear wheel into a corner.
abstract.cn: 想象新机器把旧齿轮推进墙角。

abstract.en: See a calendar page flipping until the rules turn yellow.
abstract.cn: 想象日历一页页翻过，直到规则泛黄。

abstract.en: See a dusty signboard replaced by a bright new one.
abstract.cn: 想象落灰的旧招牌被崭新招牌替换。

examples.en: New safety rules antiquated the factory's old wiring.
examples.cn: 新的安全法规使工厂的旧线路过时了。

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers both the fading of a thing and its final discarding.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: time stamping an object with the word 'old'.

definition_zh: 防腐的；杀菌的；消毒剂；冷漠超然的
definition_en: preventing the growth of disease-causing germs, or a substance that does this; also coldly impersonal
core_image: 手术室里银亮的器械和刺鼻的药水味
scene: 诊室的灯亮着，护士正把器械浸入药液。The nurse wiped the wound with antiseptic.
sceneCN: 这里 antiseptic 是「消毒剂」（第 2 个义项：用来杀菌防腐的物质）；句意为护士用消毒剂擦拭伤口。

pos.zh: （喻）冷漠超然的；无菌般洁净的

derivatives.zh: 由同根构成，义为「防腐；抗菌处理」
反义同根词，义为「感染的；脓毒的」
同根名词，义为「脓毒症；败血症」

senses.title: Preventing infection
senses.definition: describing substances or conditions that stop germs from growing and wounds from festering
senses.definitionCN: 指能阻止病菌繁殖、防止伤口化脓的物质或环境
senses.example: Antiseptic surgery dramatically cut deaths after operations.
senses.exampleCN: 无菌外科手术大幅降低了术后死亡率。
senses.why: Anti- means 'against' and septikos 'putrefying', so the word literally means 'against rot'.
senses.whyCN: anti- 表示「对抗」，septikos 意为「腐烂的」，字面即「对抗腐坏」。

senses.title: A germ-killing substance
senses.definition: a chemical applied to skin or wounds to kill or slow the growth of germs
senses.definitionCN: 涂敷于皮肤或伤口以杀灭或抑制病菌的化学制剂
senses.example: The nurse wiped the wound with antiseptic.
senses.exampleCN: 护士用消毒剂擦拭伤口。
senses.why: A word that names a quality easily names the thing carrying the quality.
senses.whyCN: 表示性质的词很容易转指带有该性质的东西。

senses.title: Coldly clean and impersonal
senses.titleCN: 冷漠超然的；无菌般洁净的
senses.definition: describing places or manners that are spotless yet strangely lifeless and unemotional
senses.definitionCN: 形容一尘不染却缺乏生气与情感的地方或态度
senses.example: The hotel lobby felt antiseptic, with no trace of anyone at home.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店大堂洁净得冷漠，没有一点生活的痕迹。
senses.why: The hospital's sterile cleanliness became the picture of any place scrubbed of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 医院无菌般的洁净，被引申为任何被擦去人情的场所的样子。

intro.en: Antiseptic pairs Greek anti 'against' with septikos 'putrefying', coined in the age of germ theory.
intro.cn: antiseptic 由希腊语 anti「对抗」与 septikos「腐烂的」组合而成，诞生于细菌理论时代。

items.en: The root *sehp- meant 'to rot, decay', giving Greek sepein 'to putrefy'.
items.cn: 词根 *sehp- 意为「腐烂」，衍生出希腊语 sepein「使腐败」。

items.en: anti meant 'against', and septikos meant 'causing putrefaction'.
items.cn: 希腊语 anti 意为「对抗」，septikos 意为「导致腐烂的」。

items.en: The English word was formed in the mid-eighteenth century from these Greek parts.
items.cn: 英语于十八世纪中叶用这两个希腊语成分构成此词。

items.en: Joseph Lister's antiseptic surgery turned the word into a milestone of medicine.
items.cn: 李斯特的抗菌外科手术使这个词成为医学里程碑。

items.en: Today the word covers real germ-killers and, by metaphor, any airless kind of cleanliness.
items.cn: 如今这个词既指真正的杀菌剂，也隐喻毫无生气的洁净。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the sepsis family and anti- words; the near-meaning group collects germ-fighters.
note.cn: 形近组收 sepsis 词族与 anti- 词；近义组收集各种杀菌之物。

normal.cn: 把 ant「蚂蚁」放在 septic 前：蚂蚁守护伤口免受病菌。

normal.en: Antiseptic acts on the skin; antibiotic acts inside the body.

normal.en: Antisepsis is the practice; antiseptic is the agent.

abstract.en: Smell the sharp sting of iodine.
abstract.cn: 想象碘酒刺鼻的气味。

abstract.en: See an empty marble corridor with no people at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一条空无一人的大理石走廊。

examples.en: Antiseptic surgery dramatically cut deaths after operations.
examples.cn: 无菌外科手术大幅降低了术后死亡率。

examples.en: The hotel lobby felt antiseptic, with no trace of anyone at home.

sensesIntro.en: One Greek pair first fights germs, then names the fight's weapon, then cools into a metaphor for sterile lifelessness.
sensesIntro.cn: 这对希腊语成分先对抗病菌，再转指对抗的武器，最后冷却为「无菌般冷漠」的隐喻。

core.cn: 核心意象：灯下银亮的器械，任何污秽都无法存活。

definition_en: a word that means the opposite of another word
core_image: 跷跷板两端坐着 hot 与 cold
scene: 黑板上并排写着两个词，中间一条分隔线。Hot is the antonym of cold.
sceneCN: 这里 antonym 是「反义词」（第 1 个义项：与另一词意义相反的词）；句意为 hot 是 cold 的反义词。

senses.title: A word of opposite meaning
senses.definition: a word whose meaning is the direct opposite of another word's meaning
senses.definitionCN: 意义与另一个词直接相反的词
senses.example: Light is the antonym of heavy in this context.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个语境里 light 是 heavy 的反义词。
senses.why: Anti- means 'opposite' and onyma 'name', so the word means 'an opposite name'.
senses.whyCN: anti- 表示「相反」，onyma 意为「名称」，合起来就是「相反的名称」。

senses.title: A member of an opposite pair
senses.definition: either word of a contrasting pair used in teaching and lexicography
senses.definitionCN: 教学与词典学中构成对照的一对词中的任何一个
senses.example: Buy and sell form a classic antonym pair.
senses.exampleCN: buy 与 sell 构成一对经典反义词。
senses.why: Opposites are rarely alone: naming one antonym invokes its twin, so the word also names the pairing itself.
senses.whyCN: 反义词很少单独存在：说出一个反义词必然唤起它的配对者，因此这个词也指配对本身。

items.en: It spread with thesauruses and vocabulary teaching in schools.

abstract.en: See a mirror that turns black into white.
abstract.cn: 想象把黑照成白的镜子。

abstract.en: See two arrows pointing away from each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两支背向而行的箭。

examples.cn: hot 是 cold 的反义词。

examples.en: Light is the antonym of heavy in this context.

examples.cn: 学生们被要求为十个形容词写出反义词。

root: 源自希腊语 anti-「相反」+ onyma「名称」（onoma 的变体）；十九世纪中叶作为 synonym 的对立术语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A single scholarly term: a name set against another name.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个学术术语：与另一个名字针锋相对的名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two names facing each other from opposite ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个名字在两端彼此相对。

branches.cn: big-small 这类可分级反义对

intro.en: A Greek compound about names and their opposites.
intro.cn: 一个关于名称及其对立面的希腊式复合词。

latinIntro.en: The -onym family names kinds of words.
latinIntro.cn: -onym 词族为各类「词」命名。

definition_zh: 冷漠的；无动于衷的；缺乏兴趣的
definition_en: showing no interest, energy, or concern
core_image: 投票日坐在沙发上一动不动的年轻人
scene: 街道上锣鼓喧天，宣传车一辆辆驶过，他却瘫在沙发里换台。Voters were apathetic about the election.
sceneCN: 这里 apathetic 是「冷漠的」（第 1 个义项：对事情缺乏兴趣与热情）；句意为选民对这次选举态度冷漠。

derivatives.zh: 由同根构成，义为「冷漠；无兴趣」
由本词加 -ally 构成，义为「冷漠地」
同缀反概念词，义为「共情；同理心」

senses.title: Showing no interest or concern
senses.definition: not interested in or caring about what is happening around you
senses.definitionCN: 对身边发生的事既不感兴趣也不在意
senses.example: Voters were apathetic about the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选民对这次选举态度冷漠。
senses.why: A- means 'without' and pathos 'feeling', so the word means 'without feeling'.
senses.whyCN: a- 表示「没有」，pathos 意为「情感」，合起来就是「没有情感」。

senses.title: Lacking energy or drive
senses.definition: slow and unmotivated, making no effort to act or change things
senses.definitionCN: 迟缓而缺乏动力，不付出努力去行动或改变
senses.example: He grew apathetic after months of job hunting.
senses.exampleCN: 找工作几个月后，他变得无精打采。
senses.why: When feeling drains away, action drains with it, so 'no feeling' slides into 'no drive'.
senses.whyCN: 情感耗尽时行动力也随之耗尽，于是「无情感」滑向「无动力」。

intro.en: Apathetic comes from Greek apatheia 'freedom from feeling', built on a- 'without' and pathos 'emotion'.
intro.cn: apathetic 来自希腊语 apatheia「无情感」，由 a-「没有」与 pathos「情感」构成。

items.en: The root *kwent(h)- meant 'to suffer', giving Greek pathos.
items.cn: 词根 *kwent(h)- 意为「承受、遭受」，衍生出希腊语 pathos。

items.en: apatheia meant absence of feeling; the Stoics praised it as freedom from passion.
items.cn: apatheia 意为「无情感」，斯多葛学派把它视为摆脱激情困扰的境界。

items.en: English borrowed apathy and then formed apathetic in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语先借入 apathy，随后在十七世纪构成 apathetic。

items.en: The word spread into politics and sociology to describe disengaged publics.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪这个词进入政治与社会学，用来描述疏离的大众。

items.en: Today apathetic criticizes both cold indifference and listless exhaustion.
items.cn: 如今 apathetic 既指冷漠无视，也指倦怠无力的状态。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pathos family; the near-meaning group gathers words for not caring.
note.cn: 形近组收 pathos 词族；近义组收表示「不在乎」的词。

entries.definition: able to share another person's feelings
entries.definitionCN: 有同理心的，与本词同根且意义相反

entries.definition: feeling or showing pity and support
the state of feeling no interest
entries.definitionCN: 冷漠；无兴趣，本词的名词形式

entries.definition: not interested in or concerned about something
lacking energy and alertness
not worried or interested

normalIntro.en: Apathetic literally means without feeling.
normalIntro.cn: apathetic 的字面义就是「没有情感」。

normal.en: a- = without; path = feeling; -etic = adjective.
normal.cn: a- 表「没有」，path 表「情感」，-etic 是形容词后缀。

normal.en: Empathy is its mirror: feeling into another person.
normal.cn: empathy 是它的镜像：感受他人之情。

normal.en: Apathetic about is the common pattern in sentences.
normal.cn: 句中最常见的搭配是 apathetic about。

normal.en: The noun apathy is shorter and very common in news.
normal.cn: 名词 apathy 更短，新闻里很常见。

normal.en: Pathos in art means stirring emotion, the opposite cure.
normal.cn: 艺术里的 pathos 指打动人的情感，恰是其反药。

abstract.en: See a grey couch with a person who never moves.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色沙发上纹丝不动的人。

abstract.en: See a phone ringing with nobody answering.
abstract.cn: 想象电话响个不停却无人接听。

abstract.en: See rain on a window that no one watches.
abstract.cn: 想象无人注视的窗上雨痕。

examples.en: Voters were apathetic about the election.
examples.cn: 选民对这次选举态度冷漠。

examples.en: He grew apathetic after months of job hunting.
examples.cn: 找工作几个月后，他变得无精打采。

examples.en: The team's apathetic performance disappointed the coach.
examples.cn: 球队无精打采的表现让教练很失望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿怕塞提克」——什么都不怕也不急，塞在原地一动不动，正是冷漠倦怠的样子。

root: 源自希腊语 apatheia「无情感」：否定前缀 a-「没有」+ pathos「情感、遭遇」+ 形容词后缀 -etic；与 sympathy、empathy 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From 'no feeling' the word moves to 'no energy', covering both cold hearts and tired ones.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「无情感」到「无动力」，这个词既写冷漠的心，也写疲惫的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shrug that answers everything.
core.cn: 核心意象：用一个耸肩回答所有事。

intro.en: A Greek negative compound about feeling.
intro.cn: 一个表示「无情感」的希腊语否定复合词。

latinIntro.en: The path- root runs through sympathy, empathy and pathology.
latinIntro.cn: path- 词根贯穿 sympathy、empathy 与 pathology。

definition_zh: 孔；缝隙；（相机）光圈；口径
definition_en: an opening, hole, or gap, especially one that lets light through
core_image: 相机镜头里一开一合的金属叶片
scene: 暗房里红光微亮，摄影师转动镜头上的圆环。A wide aperture lets in more light.
sceneCN: 这里 aperture 是「光圈」（第 2 个义项：镜头上控制进光量的开孔）；句意为大光圈能放进更多光线。

derivatives.zh: 同根词，义为「通便的；有开孔作用的」
同根借词，义为「开胃酒」（原义「打开」）

senses.title: An opening or gap
senses.definition: a hole or narrow opening in a surface or structure, especially one admitting air or light
senses.definitionCN: 表面或结构上的孔洞或窄口，尤指可透光透气的
senses.example: Light spilled through a small aperture in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 光线从墙上的一个小孔中洒进来。
senses.why: From aperire 'to open', the noun names the thing that has been opened.
senses.whyCN: 来自 aperire「打开」，名词指被打开出来的那个口子。

senses.title: The lens opening of a camera
senses.definition: the adjustable opening in a camera lens that controls how much light enters
senses.definitionCN: 相机镜头中可调节的开孔，控制进光量
senses.example: A wide aperture lets in more light.
senses.exampleCN: 大光圈能放进更多光线。
senses.why: The lens contains a literal little opening, so optics borrowed the same word for it.
senses.whyCN: 镜头里确实有一个小开口，光学借用了同一个词来称呼它。

intro.en: Aperture goes back to Latin aperire 'to open', via the Late Latin noun aperture.
intro.cn: aperture 源自拉丁语 aperire「打开」，经后期拉丁语名词 aperture 进入英语。

items.en: The root *per- meant 'to lead or pass over', the base of Latin parire.
items.cn: 词根 *per- 意为「引、过」，是拉丁语 parire 的基础。

items.en: aperire meant 'to open', as in April, the month buds open.
items.cn: aperire 意为「打开」，April（四月）即草木初开之月。

items.en: Late Latin formed apertura, 'an opening', from the verb.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语由该动词构成 apertura「开口」。

items.en: English took the word in late Middle English, first in medicine and architecture.
items.cn: 英语于中古英语晚期借入此词，最早用于医学与建筑。

items.en: Nineteenth-century photography fixed its best-known sense: the lens aperture.
items.cn: 十九世纪的摄影术确立了它最著名的义项：镜头光圈。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the aper- family; the near-meaning group gathers openings of all kinds.
note.cn: 形近组收 aper- 词族；近义组收各种「开口」。

entries.definition: a drink taken before a meal to open the appetite
entries.definitionCN: 开胃酒，同源于 aperire「打开」

entries.definition: an orange-yellow fruit
entries.definitionCN: 杏；只是词形相近，词源亦同出 aperire 一系但意义无关

entries.definition: the boundary line around a shape
entries.definitionCN: 周长；周边，词形相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a gap or hole that allows passage
an opening of the body or of a tube
an opening that lets air or gas escape

normalIntro.en: Aperture is the mouth of a camera.
normalIntro.cn: aperture 就是相机的「嘴巴」。

normal.en: Root aper- means open, as in aperitif.
normal.cn: 词根 aper- 表示「打开」，同 aperitif。

normal.en: April opens the year's flowers; aperture opens to light.
normal.cn: April 让百花开放，aperture 向光线开放。

normal.en: Wide aperture = more light; narrow aperture = less.
normal.cn: 大光圈进光多，小光圈进光少。

normal.en: Aperture priority is a standard camera mode.
normal.cn: 光圈优先是相机的标准模式。

normal.en: In building, aperture can be any window-like gap.
normal.cn: 在建筑里 aperture 可指窗状开口。

abstract.en: See metal blades folding open inside a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象镜头内金属叶片张开。

abstract.en: See a keyhole with light leaking through.
abstract.cn: 想象锁孔里漏出的一线光。

abstract.en: See a pupil widening in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室中放大的瞳孔。

examples.en: Light spilled through a small aperture in the wall.
examples.cn: 光线从墙上的一个小孔中洒进来。

examples.en: A wide aperture lets in more light.
examples.cn: 大光圈能放进更多光线。

examples.en: She adjusted the aperture before taking the shot.
examples.cn: 她在按下快门前调整了光圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿珀彻」——「阿」然「开」一口，「彻」底透进光，正是开孔透光之意。

root: 源自拉丁语 aperire「打开」（印欧词根 *per-「引、过」），经后期拉丁语 apertura「开口」于十五世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: From any physical opening the word narrowed into photography's light-controlling hole.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任何实际的开口，这个词收窄为摄影里控制进光的孔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hole that decides how much world gets in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个决定让多少世界进来的孔。

branches.en: a crack in the stone wall
an opening tuned like an eye
branches.cn: 调得像瞳孔一样的开口

intro.en: A Latin verb turned noun: open, then the opening itself.
intro.cn: 由拉丁动词转来的名词：先「打开」，再指「打开之物」。

latinIntro.en: The aper- root also gives aperitif and aperient.
latinIntro.cn: aper- 词根还派生 aperitif 与 aperient。

definition_zh: 顶点；最高点；顶峰
definition_en: the highest point or top of something
core_image: 金字塔最上面那块石头
scene: 登山队终于站上最后一块岩石，脚下群山如浪。They reached the apex of the mountain at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 apex 是「顶点」（第 1 个义项：某物的最高点）；句意为他们中午到达了山顶。

collocations.phrase: at the apex of a career

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「顶点的；顶生的」
复合词，义为「食物链顶端的捕食者」

senses.title: The topmost point of a thing
senses.definition: the very top or tip of a shape, object, or structure
senses.definitionCN: 形状、物体或结构的最上端或尖顶
senses.example: They reached the apex of the mountain at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们中午到达了山顶。
senses.why: Latin apex meant the pointed tip of a tool or roof, so the word keeps the picture of a peak.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apex 原指工具或屋顶的尖端，这个词保留了「尖峰」的画面。

senses.title: The highest or strongest point
senses.definition: the point of greatest success, power, or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 成功、权力或强度的最高点
senses.example: The novel marks the apex of her career.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说标志着她事业的巅峰。
senses.why: Whatever stands highest in space also stands highest in rank, so height became supremacy.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的最高往往也是地位上的最高，于是「高度」引申为「至尊」。

intro.en: Apex is a Latin word for a pointed tip, taken into English whole and unchanged.
intro.cn: apex 是拉丁语中表示「尖顶」的词，原形原义进入英语。

items.en: The root *h₂eḱ- meant 'sharp', the same source as acid and acute.
items.cn: 词根 *h₂eḱ- 意为「尖锐」，也是 acid 与 acute 的来源。

items.en: apex meant 'tip, point', including the pointed cap worn by priests.
items.cn: apex 意为「尖端、顶点」，也指祭司所戴的尖顶帽。

items.en: English adopted apex in the seventeenth century in geometry and anatomy.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入 apex，用于几何与解剖学。

items.en: Sciences kept it precise: the apex of a leaf, lung, or triangle.
items.cn: 科学领域沿用其精确义：叶尖、肺尖、三角顶点。

items.en: General writing now uses apex freely for any peak of achievement.
items.cn: 如今普通写作也用 apex 泛指成就的顶峰。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the sharp-root family; the near-meaning group gathers high points.
note.cn: 形近组收「尖锐」词根家族；近义组收各种「高点」。

entries.definition: relating to the apex or tip
entries.definitionCN: 顶端的；尖端的，本词的形容词形式

entries.definition: sharp in angle or mind
entries.definitionCN: 锐角的；敏锐的，同出「尖锐」词根

entries.definition: a rod on which wheels turn
entries.definitionCN: 轮轴；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the highest point, especially of a mountain or meeting
the point directly overhead; the peak of success
the highest level of achievement

normalIntro.en: Apex is the single highest point.
normalIntro.cn: apex 就是那唯一的最高点。

normal.en: Latin apex = tip; think acid and acute for the sharp root.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 apex 表尖端；联想 acid、acute 的「尖锐」词根。

normal.en: Two plurals: everyday apexes, Latin apices.
normal.cn: 两种复数：日常 apexes，拉丁式 apices。

normal.en: Apex predator is the standard ecology term.
normal.cn: apex predator 是生态学标准术语。

normal.en: Apical is the adjective in biology.
normal.cn: 生物学中形容词是 apical。

normal.en: Zenith is the sky's apex; apex fits any field.
normal.cn: zenith 是天空的顶点，apex 适用于任何领域。

abstract.en: See the last stone set on a pyramid.
abstract.cn: 想象金字塔砌上的最后一块石头。

abstract.en: See a sprinter's chest crossing the line first.
abstract.cn: 想象短跑者率先撞线的胸口。

abstract.en: See a lone eagle above every other bird.
abstract.cn: 想象高踞众鸟之上的孤鹰。

examples.en: They reached the apex of the mountain at noon.
examples.cn: 他们中午到达了山顶。

examples.en: The novel marks the apex of her career.
examples.cn: 这部小说标志着她事业的巅峰。

examples.en: Lions are apex predators on the African plain.
examples.cn: 狮子是非洲草原上的顶级掠食者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿佩克斯」——像「爱佩」之「可思」：人人爱佩之处必是可望的顶尖。

root: 直接借自拉丁语 apex「尖端、顶点」，印欧词根 *h₂eḱ-「尖锐」（同源词 acid、acute），十七世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A pointed tip in geometry grows into the peak of any achievement.
sensesIntro.cn: 几何里的尖顶，长成了任何成就的顶峰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last stone at the very top.
core.cn: 核心意象：最顶端的最后一块石。

branches.en: the one at the very top

intro.en: A bare Latin noun adopted whole into English.
intro.cn: 一个原形借入英语的光杆拉丁名词。

latinIntro.en: The sharp root *h₂eḱ- also gives acid, acute and edge.
latinIntro.cn: 「尖锐」词根 *h₂eḱ- 还派生 acid、acute 与 edge。

definition_zh: 格言；警句；隽语
definition_en: a short statement that expresses a general truth in a striking way
core_image: 一本书页边写着一行精炼的金句
scene: 书房里摊开的旧书上有一行划线的字。Actions speak louder than words is a well-known aphorism.
sceneCN: 这里 aphorism 是「格言」（第 1 个义项：用精辟语言表达普遍真理的短句）；句意为「行动胜于言辞」是句著名格言。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「格言作者；善作警句者」
由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「格言式的；精辟的」
由 aphoristic 加 -ally 构成，义为「精辟地」

senses.title: A short saying of general truth
senses.definition: a concise sentence stating a principle or truth about life
senses.definitionCN: 以简洁语句陈述人生原则或普遍真理
senses.example: Actions speak louder than words is a well-known aphorism.
senses.exampleCN: 「行动胜于言辞」是句著名格言。
senses.why: From aphorizein 'to define', the word names speech that pins truth down in one line.
senses.whyCN: 来自 aphorizein「下定义」，这个词指用一句话钉住真理的言语。

senses.title: A terse principle, especially medical
senses.definition: a compact rule or principle, in the style of Hippocrates' medical maxims
senses.definitionCN: 以希波克拉底医学箴言为典范的简练准则
senses.example: The textbook opens with the classic aphorisms of medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教科书以医学经典箴言开篇。
senses.why: Hippocrates' Aphorisms set the model: entire doctrines compressed into single lines.
senses.whyCN: 希波克拉底《箴言》树立了典范：把整套学说压缩进单句。

intro.en: Aphorism comes from Greek aphorismos 'definition, short maxim', from aphorizein 'to delimit'.
intro.cn: aphorism 来自希腊语 aphorismos「定义；短训」，动词原形 aphorizein 意为「划定界限」。

items.en: The root *dʰeh₁- meant 'to set, place', the base of horizein 'to bound'.
items.cn: 词根 *dʰeh₁- 意为「放置」，是 horizein「划定」的基础。

items.en: apo- (from) + horizein (to bound) made aphorizein, 'to mark off, define'.
items.cn: apo-（从中）+ horizein（界定）构成 aphorizein「标出、定义」。

items.en: The noun aphorismos meant a definition or concise maxim.
items.cn: 名词 aphorismos 意为定义或简练格言。

items.en: It passed through Latin aphorismus and French aphorisme into English.
items.cn: 该词经拉丁语 aphorismus 与法语 aphorisme 进入英语。

items.en: English adopted it in the sixteenth century, first for medical maxims.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入，最初指医学箴言。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the horizein family; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of sayings.
note.cn: 形近组收 horizein 词族；近义组收各类「言」。

entries.definition: the line where earth and sky seem to meet
expressed in short striking sentences
entries.definitionCN: 格言式的，本词的形容词形式

entries.definition: loss of the ability to speak
entries.definitionCN: 失语症；只是词形相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a short statement of a general rule of conduct
an old and well-known saying

definition_zh: 每个；每人；各
definition_en: to or for each one individually

scene: 面包店的纸袋排成一排，店员往每个袋里放进两块糖。The tickets cost twenty dollars apiece.
sceneCN: 这里 apiece 是「每个」（第 1 个义项：按个体逐一计算）；句意为这些票每张二十美元。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「片；块；件」
近义词，义为「每个」

senses.title: For or to each one
senses.definition: with reference to each individual item or person separately
senses.definitionCN: 就每个个体分别而言，用于逐个计价或分配
senses.example: The tickets cost twenty dollars apiece.
senses.exampleCN: 这些票每张二十美元。
senses.why: The phrase a piece literally means 'one piece', and counting by single pieces became the adverb of individual shares.
senses.whyCN: a piece 字面是「一片」，按单片计数的说法演变为表示个体份额的副词。

senses.title: With one for every member of a group
senses.definition: distributed so that every person in the group receives the same number
senses.definitionCN: 分配时使群体中每人得到相同的数量
senses.example: The children got two cookies apiece.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们每人得到两块饼干。
senses.why: Counting pieces one by one naturally counts people one by one, so the same adverb covers fair shares.
senses.whyCN: 逐片计数自然也逐人计数，于是同一个副词也用于公平的分配。

intro.en: Apiece is simply the phrase 'a piece' written together, recorded as one word by the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: apiece 就是词组 a piece 的合写，十五世纪已作为单词出现。

items.en: piece meant 'a fragment, a portion', itself from Latin *pettia.
items.cn: piece 意为「碎片；一份」，源自俗拉丁语 *pettia。

items.en: The phrase of piece or a piece meant 'each one'.
items.cn: 中古英语词组 of piece 或 a piece 表示「每一个」。

items.en: The two words fused into apiece as a single adverb.
items.cn: 两个词融合为单词 apiece，用作副词。

items.en: It became the standard way to state unit prices and shares.
items.cn: 它成为表述单价与人均份额的标准方式。

items.en: Today apiece is common in prices, rations, and statistics.
items.cn: 如今 apiece 常用于价格、配给与统计数据。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on piece; the near-meaning group gathers each-words.
note.cn: 形近组收基于 piece 的词；近义组收表示「各自」的词。

definition_zh: 远地点；（喻）最高点；鼎盛期
definition_en: the point in an orbit farthest from Earth; also the highest point of development
core_image: 卫星轨道上离地球最远的那一点
scene: 天文馆的穹幕上，一条椭圆轨道缓缓展开。The satellite reaches its apogee on the far side of its orbit.
sceneCN: 这里 apogee 是「远地点」（第 1 个义项：轨道上距地球最远的点）；句意为卫星在轨道远端到达远地点。

derivatives.zh: 反义同根词，义为「近地点」
由本词加 -an 构成，义为「远地点的」

senses.title: The farthest orbital point from Earth
senses.definition: the point in an orbit around the Earth that is farthest from the Earth's centre
senses.definitionCN: 绕地轨道上距地心最远的一点
senses.example: The satellite reaches its apogee on the far side of its orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星在轨道远端到达远地点。
senses.why: Apo- means 'away from' and ge 'earth', so the word literally means 'away from the earth'.
senses.whyCN: apo- 表示「远离」，ge 意为「地球」，字面即「离地球最远处」。

senses.title: The highest point of development
senses.definition: the farthest or highest stage that something reaches, especially of achievement or influence
senses.definitionCN: 事物达到的最远或最高阶段，尤指成就或影响力
senses.example: The empire stood at the apogee of its power.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国正处于权力的顶峰。
senses.why: The farthest point of an orbit became the picture of any farthest reach of power or art.
senses.whyCN: 轨道的最远点被引申为权力或艺术所能企及的最远处。

intro.en: Apogee comes from Greek apogaion, 'away from the earth', built on apo- 'away' and gaia/ge 'earth'.
intro.cn: apogee 来自希腊语 apogaion「离地」，由 apo-「远离」与 gaia/ge「大地」构成。

items.en: The root *ghel- or *gwhem- underlies ge, 'earth', seen in geography.
items.cn: 印欧词根构成 ge「大地」，也见于 geography。

items.en: apogaion named the point of a solar orbit farthest from earth.
items.cn: 希腊语 apogaion 指日行轨道上离地最远的点。

items.en: Greek astronomy passed the term through Arabic to medieval Latin.
items.cn: 希腊天文学术语经阿拉伯语传入中世纪拉丁语。

items.en: French apogée gave English apogee in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 apogée 于十六世纪传入英语成为 apogee。

items.en: Space science keeps the technical sense; general writing uses the figurative one.
items.cn: 航天科学沿用技术义，一般写作多用其比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the apo-/geo- family; the near-meaning group gathers high points.
note.cn: 形近组收 apo-/geo- 词族；近义组收各种「顶点」。

normal.cn: apo- 表「远离」，ge 表「大地」，与 geography 同根。

normal.en: Perigee is the opposite: near the earth.

normal.en: Apogee and perigee describe orbits around Earth.

normal.en: For other bodies, use apocenter and pericenter.

normal.en: Figuratively, apogee equals the peak of anything.

abstract.en: See an empire drawn on a map at full extent.

examples.en: Her career reached its apogee in the 1990s.

definition_zh: 封神；神化；（喻）巅峰；完美典范
definition_en: the act of raising someone or something to divine status; also the perfect example or highest point
core_image: 凡人被托上云端，走向诸神之列
scene: 壁画高处，画师给帝王加了一圈光环。The painting shows the apotheosis of the emperor.
sceneCN: 这里 apotheosis 是「神化」（第 1 个义项：把凡人抬升为神）；句意为这幅画描绘了帝王被封神的场景。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ize 构成，义为「把……神化」
形容词化用法见 apotheosized，义为「被神化的」
同根神学词，义为「成神；与神合一」

senses.title: Being made a god
senses.definition: the elevation of a person to the rank of a god, as Roman emperors were deified
senses.definitionCN: 把人提升到神的地位，如罗马皇帝被尊为神
senses.example: The painting shows the apotheosis of the emperor.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画描绘了帝王被封神的场景。
senses.why: Apo- means 'to' or 'from' and theos 'god', so the word literally means 'to place into godhood'.
senses.whyCN: apo- 表示「到／从」，theos 意为「神」，字面即「安放为神」。

senses.title: The perfect or supreme example
senses.definition: the finest or most typical instance of a quality or style
senses.definitionCN: 某种品质或风格的最完美、最典型的体现
senses.example: This dish is the apotheosis of simple cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 这道菜是简朴烹饪的极致典范。
senses.why: If mortals can rise to godhood, things can rise to perfection, so the word spread to praise.
senses.whyCN: 既然凡人能升格为神，事物也能升格为完美，这个词于是扩展为赞语。

intro.en: Apotheosis comes from Greek apotheoun 'to deify', from apo- and theos 'god'.
intro.cn: apotheosis 来自希腊语 apotheoun「封神」，由 apo- 与 theos「神」构成。

items.en: The root *deiwos- meant 'bright one', the base of theos and deity.
items.cn: 词根 *deiwos- 意为「发光者」，是 theos 与 deity 的基础。

items.en: apotheoun meant 'to make a god'; apotheosis was the act or process.
items.cn: 希腊语 apotheoun 意为「立为神」，apotheosis 指其行为或过程。

items.en: Hellenistic kings and later Roman emperors received formal apotheosis.
items.cn: 希腊化诸王及后来的罗马皇帝获得正式的封神礼遇。

items.en: The word passed through Latin apotheosis and French apotheose.
items.cn: 该词经拉丁语 apotheosis 与法语 apotheose 传承。

items.en: English took it in the sixteenth century, and by the eighteenth it praised earthly perfection too.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入，至十八世纪已用于称颂人间的极致。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the theos family; the near-meaning group gathers words for elevation and perfection.
note.cn: 形近组收 theos 词族；近义组收表示「升华与极致」的词。

definition_zh: 使惊骇；使震惊；使胆寒
definition_en: to fill someone with horror or shock
core_image: 推开房门后猛地倒吸的一口冷气
scene: 老屋的门被推开，尘土里露出塌了半边的地板。The condition of the house appalled the inspectors.
sceneCN: 这里 appall 是「使惊骇」（第 1 个义项：令人极度震惊恐惧）；句意为房屋的状况令检查人员大为震惊。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转形容词，义为「骇人的；糟糕透顶的」
由 appalling 加 -ly 构成，义为「骇人地；极糟地」
同根词，义为「（棺）罩；（使）失去吸引力」

senses.title: To fill with horror
senses.definition: to shock and horrify someone deeply
senses.definitionCN: 使某人深感震惊与恐惧
senses.example: The condition of the house appalled the inspectors.
senses.exampleCN: 房屋的状况令检查人员大为震惊。
senses.why: The old image is a pall, the dark cloth thrown over a face or coffin: horror as something laid over you like a shroud.
senses.whyCN: 古老的意象是 pall——盖在面孔或棺木上的黑布：惊骇就像一块裹尸布罩到你身上。

senses.title: To grow pale with fear
senses.definition: to turn pale or weak with dread, the older intransitive use
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧而脸色发白、浑身无力，为较早期的用法
senses.example: Her cheeks appalled at the dreadful news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到噩耗，她的双颊吓得发白。
senses.why: Pall means to grow pale, so to appall was first to blanch someone's face with fear.
senses.whyCN: pall 本指变得苍白，所以 appall 最初指吓得人脸色发白。

intro.en: Appall combines the prefix ap- (ad-, 'to') with pall, from Old English paell, a cloak or covering.
intro.cn: appall 由前缀 ap-（ad-「朝向」）加 pall 构成，pall 来自古英语 paell「斗篷；罩布」。

items.en: paell meant a rich cloak or covering cloth.
items.cn: 古英语 paell 指华贵的斗篷或罩布。

items.en: pall named the cloth draped over coffins and chalices.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 pall 指覆盖棺木与圣杯的罩布。

items.en: The verb pall meant 'to cloak' and then 'to grow pale or tiresome'.
items.cn: 动词 pall 先指「披罩」，后指「变得苍白或令人厌倦」。

items.en: Middle English formed appallen, 'to grow pale with horror'.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 appallen「吓得脸色发白」。

items.en: Today the transitive sense dominates: to appall someone; the adjective appalling is the commonest form.
items.cn: 如今及物义占主导：使某人惊骇；形容词 appalling 最为常用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pall family; the near-meaning group gathers words of horror.
note.cn: 形近组收 pall 词族；近义组收表示「惊骇」的词。

entries.definition: a coffin cloth; to become dull or tiresome
entries.definitionCN: 棺罩；（乐趣）衰减，本词的同根词

entries.definition: unusually pale in colour
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的；与拉丁 pallere「苍白」相关，词义呼应

entries.definition: an earnest request or attraction
entries.definitionCN: 呼吁；吸引力；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to fill with horror
to fill with worry and disappointment
entries.definitionCN: 使惊愕；使沮丧，惊中带愁

entries.definition: to surprise and upset strongly

normalIntro.en: Appall throws a dark pall over the mind.
normalIntro.cn: appall 就像往心头罩一块黑布。

normal.en: ap- (to) + pall (cover) = throw a cover over.
normal.cn: ap-（朝向）加 pall（罩布），即「罩住」。

normal.en: Two l's in American spelling: appall, appalling.
normal.cn: 美式拼写双写 l：appall、appalling。

normal.en: Appalling is far more common than the verb.
normal.cn: appalling 比动词原形常用得多。

normal.en: Be appalled at/by is the standard pattern.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 be appalled at/by。

normal.en: Pall as a verb means the pleasure fades.
normal.cn: pall 作动词指兴致渐消。

abstract.en: See a black cloth dropped over a cage.
abstract.cn: 想象黑布罩住鸟笼。

abstract.en: See a face draining of colour.
abstract.cn: 想象脸色一寸寸变白。

abstract.en: See a door opening onto wreckage.
abstract.cn: 想象推门见到一片狼藉。

examples.en: The condition of the house appalled the inspectors.
examples.cn: 房屋的状况令检查人员大为震惊。

examples.en: Her cheeks appalled at the dreadful news.
examples.cn: 听到噩耗，她的双颊吓得发白。

examples.en: They were appalled by the waste of food.
examples.cn: 他们对食物的浪费感到震惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄怕」——「厄」运临头，「怕」得脸色发白，正是惊骇之态。

root: 中古英语 appallen「吓得发白」，由前缀 ap-（ad-「朝向」）+ pall「罩布、棺衣」（古英语 paell「斗篷」）构成；比喻惊骇如黑布罩身。

sensesIntro.en: From a covering cloth came paling cheeks, then deep horror.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块罩布，到吓得发白的脸颊，再到深深的惊骇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shroud thrown over the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块裹尸布罩上面孔。

intro.en: An English verb of covering, built with the Latin-looking prefix ad-.
intro.cn: 一个表示「罩住」的英语动词，配上前缀 ad-。

latinIntro.en: The pall- family in English mixes the cloth word and Latin pallor.
latinIntro.cn: 英语 pall- 词族混合了罩布义与拉丁语的苍白义。

definition_zh: 鬼魂；幽灵；（意外）显现
definition_en: a ghost or ghostly figure; an unexpected and striking appearance
core_image: 雾夜里走廊尽头一闪而过的白影
scene: 古堡的走廊空无一人，烛火忽然低了一低。The watchman swore he saw an apparition on the stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 apparition 是「幽灵」（第 1 个义项：如鬼魂般的显现形象）；句意为守夜人发誓在楼梯上看到了幽灵。

derivatives.zh: 同根基础词，义为「出现；显得」
同根词，义为「出现；外貌」
同根词，义为「明显的；表面上的」

senses.title: A ghost or ghostly figure
senses.definition: the spirit of a dead person appearing to the living, or any ghostlike shape
senses.definitionCN: 向活人显现的亡魂，或任何鬼魅般的形象
senses.example: The watchman swore he saw an apparition on the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 守夜人发誓在楼梯上看到了幽灵。
senses.why: From appear: what shows itself when nothing should be there earns a special word.
senses.whyCN: 源于 appear「出现」：本不该有什么却显形的东西，值得一个专门的词。

senses.title: A sudden striking appearance
senses.definition: an unexpected or remarkable appearance of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物出人意料或令人惊叹的现身
senses.example: Her apparition at the party stunned the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 她在派对上的意外现身惊呆了宾客。
senses.why: Because a ghost is defined by its appearance, the word widened to any startling arrival.
senses.whyCN: 既然幽灵以「显形」定义，这个词便扩展到一切惊人的现身。

intro.en: Apparition comes from Latin apparitio 'an appearing', from apparere 'to appear'.
intro.cn: apparition 来自拉丁语 apparitio「显现」，动词 apparere 意为「出现」。

items.en: The root *per- meant 'to lead forth', the base of parere 'to come forth'.
items.cn: 词根 *per- 意为「引出」，是 parere「生出、出现」的基础。

items.en: apparere meant 'to come into view', ap- plus parere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 apparere 意为「进入视野」，由 ap- 加 parere 构成。

items.en: apparitio named an appearance, especially a divine or ghostly one.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 apparitio 指显形，尤指神明或亡魂之显。

items.en: English adopted the word for visions and ghosts in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪借入，用于幻象与鬼魂。

items.en: The ghost sense dominates, with a refined figurative use for striking arrivals.
items.cn: 如今鬼魂义占主导，比喻义则用于惊人的现身。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the appear family; the near-meaning group gathers ghost words.
note.cn: 形近组收 appear 词族；近义组收表示「鬼魂」的词。

entries.definition: the act of coming into view; outward look
entries.definitionCN: 出现；外貌，本词的同根普通名词

entries.definition: clearly seen or understood; seeming
entries.definitionCN: 明显的；表面上的，同根形容词

entries.definition: a set of equipment
entries.definitionCN: 器械；装置；只是拼写相近，词根不同

entries.definition: a ghost or imagined figure
a frightening ghost
a ghost or shadowy likeness of someone
entries.definitionCN: 鬼影；人将死时的显形，文学用语

normalIntro.en: An apparition is something that appears when it should not.
normalIntro.cn: apparition 就是「不该出现时的现身」。

normal.en: ap- + par = come forth; same root as appear.
normal.cn: ap- 加 par 表示「出现」，与 appear 同根。

normal.en: The -ition ending marks the act of appearing.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ition 标示「显现」这一行为。

normal.en: Ghost stories live on this word.
normal.cn: 鬼故事离不开这个词。

normal.en: Figuratively, an apparition is a startling arrival.
normal.cn: 比喻义指令人惊讶的现身。

normal.en: Do not confuse with apparatus, the equipment word.
normal.cn: 不要与表器械的 apparatus 混淆。

abstract.en: See a pale figure at the end of a corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊尽头的苍白身影。

abstract.en: See candlelight bending as a door opens.
abstract.cn: 想象门开时烛火的摇曳。

abstract.en: See a famous face stepping in unannounced.
abstract.cn: 想象名人不打招呼忽然现身。

examples.en: The watchman swore he saw an apparition on the stairs.
examples.cn: 守夜人发誓在楼梯上看到了幽灵。

examples.en: Her apparition at the party stunned the guests.
examples.cn: 她在派对上的意外现身惊呆了宾客。

examples.en: In the fog, the tower looked like an apparition.
examples.cn: 雾中，那座塔宛如幽灵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆锐省」——阿婆的魂灵锐利地惊醒世人，正是幽灵显形。

root: 源自拉丁语 apparitio「显现」，动词 apparere「出现」（ap- + parere「生出、显形」，印欧词根 *per-「引出」），十五世纪经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of appearing, sharpened into ghosts and startling entrances.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「出现」的动词，被磨尖成鬼魂与惊人之现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape standing where nothing should stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：本无一物之处立着一个身影。

branches.en: a figure on a moonlit stair
there one moment, gone the next

intro.en: A Latin action-noun built on a verb of appearing.
intro.cn: 以「出现」动词为基础的拉丁式行为名词。

latinIntro.en: The par- root also gives parent, transparent and appearance.
latinIntro.cn: par- 词根还派生 parent、transparent 与 appearance。

definition_zh: 安抚；平息；满足；姑息
definition_en: to calm someone's anger by giving in or making concessions
core_image: 递上一块糖，让哭闹的孩子安静下来
scene: 婴儿的哭声在车厢里回荡，母亲轻拍着他的背。A bottle of warm milk appeased the crying baby.
sceneCN: 这里 appease 是「安抚」（第 1 个义项：用让步使怒气或不满平息）；句意为一瓶温奶安抚了哭闹的婴儿。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「安抚；绥靖」
现在分词转形容词，义为「安抚性的」
同根近义词，义为「使平静；镇压平定」

senses.title: To calm by giving in
senses.definition: to make someone less angry by agreeing to their demands or offering something
senses.definitionCN: 通过答应要求或给予东西使人息怒
senses.example: A bottle of warm milk appeased the crying baby.
senses.exampleCN: 一瓶温奶安抚了哭闹的婴儿。
senses.why: Pax means peace; the word pictures handing something over until peace returns.
senses.whyCN: pax 意为「和平」；这个词描绘的是交出些什么直到和平归来的画面。

senses.title: To satisfy a hunger or need
senses.definition: to relieve a strong desire or appetite by fulfilling it
senses.definitionCN: 通过满足来缓解强烈的欲望或需求
senses.example: A thick stew appeased their hunger after the march.
senses.exampleCN: 急行军后，一碗浓汤缓解了他们的饥饿。
senses.why: Hungry feelings behave like angry ones, so feeding and soothing share the verb.
senses.whyCN: 饥饿感的表现如同愤怒，于是「喂饱」与「抚慰」共用一个动词。

senses.title: To concede to an aggressor
senses.definition: to make political concessions to an aggressive power in hope of avoiding war
senses.definitionCN: 为避免战争而对侵略性政权作出政治让步
senses.example: The 1938 agreement is now remembered as appeasement.
senses.exampleCN: 1938 年的协定如今被记作绥靖的典型。
senses.why: Calming one aggressor scaled up from nursery to statecraft, with a bitter aftertaste.
senses.whyCN: 哄孩子的「安抚」放大为国家间的「绥靖」，且带上苦涩的贬义。

intro.en: Appease comes from Old French apaisier, from a- and pais 'peace', Latin pax.
intro.cn: appease 来自古法语 apaisier，由 a- 加 pais「和平」（拉丁语 pax）构成。

items.en: The root *peh₂k- meant 'to fasten', giving Latin pax, a binding agreement.
items.cn: 词根 *peh₂k- 意为「系结」，衍生出拉丁语 pax「缔结的和平」。

items.en: pax meant peace, originally a treaty bond.
items.cn: pax 意为和平，原指条约纽带。

items.en: apaisier meant 'to pacify, calm'.
items.cn: 古法语 apaisier 意为「使平息」。

items.en: Middle English adopted apesen in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语于十三世纪借入 apesen。

items.en: After 1938 appeasement also carries the political charge of conceding to aggression.
items.cn: 1938 年之后，appeasement 亦带上了向侵略让步的政治贬义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pax family; the near-meaning group gathers calming words.
note.cn: 形近组收 pax 词族；近义组收表示「安抚」的词。

entries.definition: the act of appeasing, especially politically
entries.definitionCN: 安抚；绥靖，本词的名词形式

entries.definition: peaceful, calming
entries.definitionCN: 和平的；温和的，同出 pax

entries.definition: hand-clapping approval
entries.definitionCN: 掌声；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to calm or bring peace, often by force
to make someone less angry
to soften someone's anger or anxiety

normalIntro.en: Appease means to bring peace by giving something.
normalIntro.cn: appease 就是「给出些什么换来平静」。

normal.en: a- + pais (peace) = make peace.
normal.cn: a- 加 pais（和平），即「求和」。

normal.en: Pax is the root of pacific and pacify too.
normal.cn: pax 也是 pacific 与 pacify 的词根。

normal.en: Appease a baby, a mob, or an appetite.
normal.cn: 可以安抚婴儿、人群，也可满足胃口。

normal.en: Appeasement in history means conceding to aggressors.
normal.cn: 历史语境中 appeasement 指对侵略者让步。

normal.en: Keep one e in the middle: appease, appeased.
normal.cn: 中间保持单 e：appease、appeased。

abstract.en: See a storm settling into still water.
abstract.cn: 想象风暴平息成静水。

root: 源自古法语 apaisier「使平息」：a- + pais「和平」（拉丁语 pax，印欧词根 *peh₂k-「系结」），十三世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One peace-word covers soothing a baby, feeding hunger, and dangerous political concession.

a meal after a long road
